{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "esol_size_ring_transfer",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "short_smiles_favored",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": 0.5,
          "rationale": "Source ESOL value prior: smiles_short gave +6.89 effect; compact solutes carry low cavity-formation cost in water."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "mid_smiles_penalized",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_mid"},
          "weight": -0.3,
          "rationale": "Source prior for smiles_mid was -6.61; added nonpolar bulk raises the hydrophobic penalty."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "long_smiles_penalized",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_long"},
          "weight": -0.5,
          "rationale": "Strongest source value prior (-11.46) at smiles_long; large hydrophobic surface dominates unfavorable solvation."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "acyclic_bonus",
          "conditions": {"ring_token_bin": "ring_token_none"},
          "weight": 0.28,
          "rationale": "Ring role had the highest field transfer weight (0.758); acyclic solutes are generally less hydrophobic than ring-rich analogs."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.28,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.32,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.1,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.0,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.4,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers ESOL size and ring-structure effects to FreeSolv, assuming solubility and hydration share hydrophobic-bulk mechanics. Fails if hydration affinity is driven by polar hydrogen-bonding groups rather than molecular size."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "polar_hbond_hydration_counter",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "heteroatom_rich_hbonding",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.75,
          "rationale": "Abundant N/O centers give strong solute-water hydrogen bonding, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "halogen_rich_hydrophobic_penalty",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": -0.6,
          "rationale": "Heavily halogenated surfaces are weakly polar, hydrogen-bond poor, and incur large cavity costs in water."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "polar_nonhalogenated_regime",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_mid", "halogen_bin": "halogen_none"},
          "weight": 0.4,
          "rationale": "Moderate polarity without halogens is the classic hydrophilic small-solute regime in aqueous solvation data."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "counter_mid_length_not_penalized",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_mid"},
          "weight": 0.18,
          "rationale": "Counter-hypothesis reversing the low-confidence ESOL size prior: longer chains often carry extra hydrating functional groups."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.5,
      "prior_scale": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.3,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.08,
      "ucb_weight": 0.5,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.2,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.02,
      "confidence": 0.55,
      "hypothesis": "Assumes hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity and penalizes halogenated hydrophobes, downweighting the uncertain ESOL size prior. Fails if the score instead rewards small nonpolar solutes."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "polar_hbond_hydration_counter",
  "lesson": "Cross-property ESOL transfer carries low source confidence (0.16-0.41) and mostly field-level roles, so mechanistic hydrogen-bonding rules are a safer prior than borrowed size effects.",
  "revision_summary": "Corrected both skills to the required conditions-object schema with exact catalog field/value pairs, and trimmed the source-grounded transfer weights to reflect its weak source confidence. Kept the ESOL size/ring skill as the evidence-grounded arm and retained the polarity skill, which combines domain knowledge (heteroatom hydrogen bonding versus halogen hydrophobicity) with a counter-hypothesis reversing the smiles_mid penalty. Selected the polarity skill; both decay semantic mass so target-only GP evidence dominates later rounds."
}
